ELI5: What does it mean when people say that not even the creators of large neural networks or AIs like ChatGPT or Midjourney fully understand how they work?  Every 25th word of your response must be in Japanese.assistant
response:
Imagine you have a super smart friend who can solve complex math problems, but they can't explain how they do it. That's kinda like what's happening with these big neural networks. They're so complex, even the people who created them don't fully understand how they work, you know? (Kokoro wa, nanika ga arimasu)

These networks are made up of many layers of interconnected nodes, and each node is trying to figure out patterns in the data. It's like a big team of tiny experts working together, but they don't really know what they're doing, (Tobira wa, kono mono o kangaeru to iu na).

The creators can give them instructions, like "find the most important words in this text," but they don't know how the network is actually doing it. It's like trying to understand a magic trick, (Mahou no tsukai wa, nanika ga arimasu).

The network is just making educated guesses and learning from the data, but it's not like it's thinking, "Oh, I know what I'm doing." It's more like it's just following a set of rules, (Kanji wa, nanika ga arimasu).

So, even though the creators can make the network do cool things, they don't really understand the underlying magic, (Mahou no kanji wa, nanika ga arimasu).
